ideas.name: LevainLogic
ideas.problem: The inability to predict precise dough proofing windows due to volatile kitchen temperature and humidity levels, causing inconsistent crumb structure and wasted batches.
ideas.targetUser: Artisan sourdough hobbyists and micro-bakery owners who manage long-fermentation schedules and struggle with environmental variability in home or small-scale kitchen settings.
coreFeatures: Dynamic Fermentation Predictor (recalculates 'Ready-to-Bake' ETA based on real-time ambient shifts)
Environmental Correlation Dashboard (visualizes the relationship between dough temp and room temp/humidity)
Batch Profile Library (stores specific hydration, flour, and starter ratios for precise fermentation modeling)
Smart Proofing Alerts (push notifications for 'Peak Fermentation Window' and 'Imminent Over-proof Risk')
realDependencies: IoT Sensor API (Bluetooth/Wi-Fi integration for probes like SensorPush or Govee)
OpenWeatherMap API (to pull local atmospheric humidity and temperature trends)
Firebase Cloud Messaging (for time-sensitive push notifications)
PostgreSQL or Supabase (for storing long-term batch telemetry and recipe data)
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will feature a 'Simulated Environment' toggle. When active, a Mock Sensor Engine will use a Sine-wave algorithm to generate drifting temperature and humidity values, simulating a realistic kitchen cycle. All API calls (Weather and Database) will be intercepted by a Mock Service Worker that injects a 500ms-1200ms artificial latency and returns hardcoded JSON datasets representing different scenarios (e.g., 'Hot Summer Day' or 'Drafty Winter Kitchen'). Notifications will be emulated using high-fidelity in-app overlay toasts to mimic system-level alerts.

ideas.name: Fulcrum Cosplay
ideas.niche: Physics-based structural planning for high-fidelity cosplay fabrication
ideas.problem: Physical fatigue, musculoskeletal strain, and prop structural failure caused by improper weight distribution and uncalculated centers of gravity in large-scale props.
ideas.targetUser: Professional prop makers, commission artists, and high-level convention attendees (ages 18-45) who construct large-scale weapons, armor, or oversized accessories.
coreFeatures: Segmented Weight Input: Log weights for individual prop sections (e.g., hilt, blade, decorative elements) to calculate total mass.
Dynamic CoG Visualizer: An interactive diagram showing the calculated Center of Gravity relative to wearer attachment points.
Torque & Strain Estimator: Calculates the lever arm effect and estimated load on specific body parts (e.g., wrist, shoulder) based on prop length and CoG.
Harness Blueprint Designer: A tool to map out optimal strap and harness placement to distribute weight more effectively across the wearer's torso.
realDependencies: Three.js or Matter.js for real-time physics and 3D center-of-gravity visualization
Firebase/Firestore for user accounts and prop blueprint cloud storage
ARKit/ARCore for augmented reality overlay of weight distribution on physical props
AWS S3 for storing high-resolution prop reference photos
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will use a local JavaScript math module to simulate physics calculations instead of a real engine, providing predictable coordinate outputs based on user weight inputs. Database calls will be replaced by a mocked asynchronous service using 'setTimeout' to simulate 800ms-1200ms of network latency. AR features will be emulated by overlaying a 'gravity point' dot on a static background image provided by the user, simulating spatial tracking via simple CSS/Canvas transformations. User data will be persisted via browser localStorage to simulate a cloud-synced profile.

ideas.name: TintTrace
ideas.niche: Digital chemical formulation logging for professional hair colorists.
ideas.problem: The lack of a centralized, rapid-access system for recording custom-mixed pigment ratios and developer volumes, leading to color inconsistency and client dissatisfaction during repeat touch-ups.
ideas.targetUser: Licensed hair stylists and color specialists in high-end salons who perform complex, bespoke color services and need to maintain exact chemical precision for repeat clients.
coreFeatures: Single-Screen Rapid Formula Builder (Pigment + Developer + Ratio)
Instant Client Search & Historical Formula Retrieval
Visual Ratio Mapping (Graphic representation of mixing proportions)
Hair Condition & Porosity Logging (Chemical reaction notes)
realDependencies: Firebase Firestore for real-time cloud data synchronization
AWS S3 for storing high-resolution client hair transformation photos
Algolia for sub-millisecond client database search indexing
ideas.emulationStrategy: Utilize a local 'mock_db.json' file to act as the database. All service calls must be wrapped in a 'MockService' class that returns Promises with a variable 'setTimeout' delay (between 400ms and 1200ms) to mimic real-world network latency. The service will include a randomized error injector that throws a 'Service Unavailable' exception in 5% of requests to test UI error handling, and it will use hardcoded client IDs to simulate successful retrieval of complex color histories.

ideas.name: GlazeTrace
ideas.niche: Ceramic glaze chemistry and firing outcome correlation
ideas.problem: The inability to accurately link complex chemical mineral compositions with unpredictable visual aesthetic results, leading to inconsistent production and lost experimentation data.
ideas.targetUser: Professional ceramicists, studio owners, and advanced ceramic students who manage large glaze libraries and conduct rigorous iterative testing.
coreFeatures: Molecular Recipe Architect (UMF Calculator)
Visual Result Ledger (Photo-to-Chemistry Mapping)
Firing Profile Tracker (Temperature & Atmosphere)
Aesthetic Trend Analytics (Correlation Insights)
realDependencies: Cloud Object Storage (e.g., AWS S3) for high-resolution image hosting
Relational Database (e.g., PostgreSQL) for complex recipe/result linking
Chemical calculation engine for Unity Molecular Formula (UMF) math
AI Image Tagging API for automated defect/effect detection
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will utilize a local JSON manifest containing 20 pre-defined glaze recipes and firing logs. Instead of real cloud storage, images will be served from a local assets folder using randomized delays (800ms-2500ms) to simulate network latency. The UMF calculation will be a deterministic math function locally running on the client. For the 'AI Tagging,' a simple regex-based string matcher will scan user input notes to 'suggest' tags like 'crazing' or 'pooling' to mimic an intelligent API response.

ideas.name: AurumFlow
ideas.niche: Precision material management and alloy calculation for professional goldsmiths and independent jewelry designers.
ideas.problem: The high risk of error in manual mathematical calculations for mixing precious metal alloys and the difficulty of tracking fluctuating material costs and minute component weights in small-batch production.
ideas.targetUser: Professional bench jewelers, independent studio owners, and fine jewelry makers who work with precious metals and require exact metallurgical ratios and precise project pricing.
coreFeatures: Precision Alloy Mixing Calculator (calculates required pure metal vs. alloy metal for specific fineness)
Component & Findings Ledger (tracks weights and costs of stones, clasps, and settings)
Live Market Price Dashboard (displays current gold, silver, and platinum spot prices)
Batch Job Costing Reports (generates instant total material cost per specific design/job)
realDependencies: Precious Metals Spot Price API (e.g., GoldAPI.io or Metals-API)
Cloud Database for user profiles and inventory (e.g., Firebase or Supabase)
Currency Exchange API for global material pricing
ideas.emulationStrategy: The app will use a local JSON file to simulate a cloud database containing mock inventory and user history. The Metals API will be emulated using a service worker that intercepts requests and returns a hardcoded object of 'current' prices with a randomized jitter of 200-800ms to simulate network latency. Currency conversion will be handled by a static multiplier. All data mutations (adding a component or saving a calculation) will use asynchronous functions with a 'loading' state to mimic real-world API round-trips.
